questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are in a crash, stop immediately and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Check if anyone is hurt. Call 911 if needed. Report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Legal if you use voice-to-text technology.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is against the law in Washington State. Texting distracts you from driving and can result in a ticket.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as well in the dark.
Rain is more likely at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less of the road around you. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop safely within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: This sign warns you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a winding road with three or more curves is coming.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what the crossing guard tells you to do.
Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the crossing guard tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a crossing guard, sign, or police officer tells you to. Always drive carefully in a school zone.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Only if other cars are nearby.
Always. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
Only while you are making the move, not before.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always. It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Signal your turn or lane change well in advance. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb to alert other drivers.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop immediately. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop serious bleeding. Wait for emergency responders.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signaling helps other drivers know what you are doing and prevents accidents.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, pull over to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: If you drive a car registered in Washington State, you must:

options.text: Have liability insurance and carry proof of it.
Carry insurance only if you ride a motorcycle or drive a large truck.
Carry insurance only if you are under 18.
Carry insurance only if your car is less than five years old.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have liability insurance and carry proof of it.
questions.explanation: All drivers in Washington State must have liability insurance and carry proof of it at all times.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive past the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to scare them so they will not cross against red lights again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make turning harder, increase stopping distance, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Is it legal to use a hand-held cell phone to make a call while driving?

options.text: Yes, it is safer than using a hands-free phone.
Yes, but only for teenage drivers.

questions.explanation: It is illegal in Washington State to use a hand-held cell phone while driving. If you need to make a call, pull over safely and stop first.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take steps to make night driving safer for yourself and others.

questions.question: How serious is the problem of drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: It is a minor traffic safety problem.
It is a serious traffic safety problem.
It is safe if you have only had a few drinks.
It is only dangerous to the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a serious traffic safety problem.
questions.explanation: Driving while impaired or intoxicated is a serious traffic safety problem. Safe driving is not possible when you drink alcohol or use drugs. It is dangerous to you and to others on the road.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and very dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign prohibiting it.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Never stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. Never swerve across lanes at the last second. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This circular sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. Watch for trains and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make gestures to show your disapproval.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make obscene gestures.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect driving ability in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight has the same effect as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.
